To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the click value of a word is highly affected by the topic and the temporal trend of news articles, 2. the click value varies across topics and temporal trends, 3. words with high click value are not necessarily the most frequent words in headlines, 4. words with high word frequency are not necessarily the words with high click values, 5. the click value is not necessarily correlated with word frequency or word length.

(i) the click-value of a word depends on its topical context, (ii) click-value of words is affected by the temporal context of the news article, (iii) click-value of a headline is affected by the topical and temporal context of the headline, (iv) the click-value can be predicted with reasonable accuracy, and (v) the click-value prediction can be used to improve headline generation.

(1) words that have high click-value in a headline tend to be nouns, and (2) words that have low click-value tend to be verbs, and (3) the click-value of a word is affected by the topic of the headline, and (4) the click-value is also affected by the topic distribution in the body of news.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how to craft better headlines for online news outlets.
the problem of identifying the most important words in news headlines.
the problem of predicting click-through rates of online news headlines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed model can effectively leverage clicks to identify words that will generate more future clicks.
the proposed method, headline click-based model, can be used to identify good headlines for a news article, and can also be applied to detect changes in user interest within topics.
the click-through rate of headlines depends on both the topical context and the linguistic attributes, which can be modeled using a generative model, HCTM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
by leveraging click data we can improve headline generation and selection, and by leveraging topic models we can improve headline click prediction.

we have developed a novel generative topic model, HCTM, that jointly models topics and click-through information to predict click-value of words for news headlines, which can be used for both full headline and good headline tasks.

we can use the valuable resource of click-through data to identify words that are more likely to attract users' attention and generate more clicks, and that we can use this click information to model topics and identify changes in user interests.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by jointly taking the topical context of news articles and the click-through information of headlines into account, we can significantly boost the performance of headline retrieval and selection tasks.
by jointly modeling topics and clicks we can identify words with high click-value that are likely to attract more users' attention.

click-through data can be used to improve news headlines and that our proposed model is able to capture the click-value of individual terms and to model the effect of topical and temporal context on click-through rate.
